description: Managing IT projects through all ten knowledge areas, from charter to closure, with the quantitative tools of scheduling, cost and risk and the agile practices that modern software teams use. Taught to the depth of the professional project management body of knowledge.
modelledOn: PMI, A Guide to the Project Management Body of Knowledge (PMBOK, 6th and 7th editions)
Scrum Guide and the Agile Practice Guide
outcomes: Explain the project life cycle, process groups and the role of the project manager in an IT organisation.
Write a project charter, scope statement and work breakdown structure for an IT project.
Build a network diagram, compute the critical path and PERT estimates, and resource-level a schedule.
Estimate and control costs with earned value management.
Plan quality, resources, communications and stakeholder engagement for a project.
Identify, analyse and respond to risks quantitatively and qualitatively, and apply agile methods where they fit.

units.title: Project management context and processes
topics: Projects, programmes and portfolios; the triple constraint and beyond
The project life cycle; process groups: initiating, planning, executing, monitoring and controlling, closing
Organisational structures, PMO, the project manager's skills; why IT projects fail (Standish, local cases)
Predictive, iterative, incremental, agile and hybrid approaches
Project management software: MS Project, OpenProject, Jira

units.title: Integration management
topics: Business case and benefits; the project charter
The project management plan and subsidiary plans
Directing and managing work; integrated change control; configuration management
Closing a project or phase; lessons learned

units.title: Scope management
topics: Collecting requirements: interviews, workshops, prototypes, user stories
Scope statement; the work breakdown structure and WBS dictionary
Validating and controlling scope; scope creep and gold plating
Product backlogs and scope in agile projects

units.title: Time management: networks, CPM and PERT
topics: Defining and sequencing activities; dependencies, leads and lags; precedence diagrams
Estimating durations: analogous, parametric, three-point, bottom-up
Critical path method: forward and backward pass, float, critical path
PERT: expected durations, variance, probability of meeting a deadline
Gantt charts, milestones, baselines; crashing and fast-tracking; resource levelling
Velocity, sprints and release planning in agile

units.title: Cost management
topics: Cost estimating techniques and accuracy ranges; cost of software (function points, COCOMO in brief)
Budgeting: cost baseline, contingency and management reserves, cash flow
Earned value management: PV, EV, AC, CV, SV, CPI, SPI, EAC, ETC, TCPI
Worked example: a university management system budget in cedis

units.title: Quality management
topics: Quality planning, assurance and control; cost of quality
Tools: cause-and-effect diagrams, Pareto charts, control charts, checklists, flowcharts
Software quality: reviews, testing, defect metrics; ISO 9001 and CMMI in brief
Definition of done and continuous improvement

units.title: Resource management
topics: Resource planning, responsibility assignment matrix (RACI), organisational charts
Acquiring, developing and managing the team; Tuckman stages, motivation, conflict
Leadership styles and virtual teams
Managing physical resources and procurement in brief: contracts, vendors, outsourcing

units.title: Communications management
topics: Communication planning: who needs what, when, how; the communications matrix
Status reports, dashboards, meetings that work; information distribution
Communication across cultures and with non-technical sponsors
Collaboration tools and documentation

units.title: Risk management
topics: Risk planning; identification techniques: brainstorming, checklists, SWOT, assumptions analysis
Qualitative analysis: probability-impact matrix, risk register
Quantitative analysis: expected monetary value, decision trees, sensitivity, Monte Carlo simulation
Responses: avoid, mitigate, transfer, accept, exploit; contingency plans; monitoring risks
Common IT risks: requirements change, technology, vendors, security, power and connectivity

units.title: Stakeholder management and capstone
topics: Identifying stakeholders; power-interest grids; engagement assessment
Managing expectations, sponsors, users and resistance; change management
Professional responsibility and ethics in project management
Capstone: a full project plan (charter, WBS, schedule, budget, risk register, communications plan) for a real IT project
